Alexandra — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (sales ops) and Jonas (revops) for the runbook and Kimberly for legal redline implications.

Short answer up front: we have an internal ops checklist and a one‑page summary we normally provide to procurement; attaching a draft ops checklist and a short explainer. High‑level notes below; please see attachments for the full checklist and a redline PDF with the callouts.

High level:
- Cap/Floor semantics: cap = monthly bill cap (hard cap per invoice) that prevents charges beyond a set amount; floor = minimum committed spend that triggers true‑up if usage is below committed units.
- Trigger detection: usage is evaluated daily and rolled into a weekly dashboard; threshold crossing is flagged in RevOps and a ticket auto‑created for the customer owner.
- Mid‑window cap hit: we first (A) attempt to burst via reserved burst capacity (if configured), (B) fall back to the next compatible model variant (cost‑optimized), then (C) return an overage estimate to procurement for reconciliation.
- True‑up cadence: quarterly true‑up by default; monthly true‑up is available if the contract specifies.

Next steps: Ben & Jonas, can you confirm runbook attachment aligns with our operational practice and update the two sections below: (1) ‘Operational escalation’ and (2) ‘Billing reconciliation steps’. Kimberly — note two legal flags in Pricing_Exhibit_v3 where we should clarify language about automatic fallback to cheaper variants.

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, Sales (Redwood Inference)

Thanks Rachel — attaching a populated ops checklist with step owners and SR ticket templates. I added an internal note on SLA exceptions and a recommended notification cadence for Greenline (daily summary + immediate alert on threshold).

Operational clarifications I added: 
1) Threshold detection logic: rolling 7‑day window on per‑customer token consumption; flag at 90% of band for pre‑emptive notice.
2) Mid‑billing window behavior: we will not silently downgrade without customer consent unless the contract explicitly permits automatic fallback. Instead we: (a) provision a temporary burst (if available), (b) notify procurement and recommend model fallback with explicit consent via the console or a signed addendum; (c) if customer requests immediate continuation and burst not available, we invoice per overage rates described in Exhibit C.
3) Billing reconciliation: RevOps will post a provisional invoice with comments and a true‑up line item for the next billing cycle if requested.

Alexandra — are you OK with the conservative approach (no silent downgrade)? If you need automatic fallback, Kimberly flagged required redline language to permit it.

Best,
